output.title: Canonical records before you automate
output.body:
If you want to automate a workflow, start with one design question: which record is canonical? In plain English, that means deciding which system is the single source of truth for one repeating process — customer details, invoices, orders, or support tickets — before you touch any automation.

The reason is simple. If three tools all “own” the same field, you do not have an AI problem yet. You have a record-control problem. The giveaway is re-keying, re-checking, or an owner having to approve the same thing twice because the data does not match.

A practical next step is to map one workflow on paper. List the manual entry points, note which tool currently holds each field, and mark where decisions stop because the records diverge. Then separate the cause into two buckets: technical issues like format or API limits, and organisational issues like data ownership or human review gates. The fix is different in each case.

If the inputs are mostly text, extraction and verification can be worth testing. That is limited to text-based inputs; PDF/scan ingestion and OCR are not implemented here, and scan-heavy workflows stay out of scope. If the records are already structured and synced, AI is probably not the first lever. Either way, keep the owner in the approval loop for any high-risk decision. The spreadsheet will survive without drama if you don’t let it improvise.
